overview: Copart operates the leading online marketplace for salvage and total-loss vehicles, connecting sellers -- primarily insurance companies -- with a global base of buyers (dismantlers, rebuilders, exporters, and dealers) through its proprietary VB3 virtual bidding auction platform. The company owns/operates a network of roughly 250+ vehicle storage and auction facilities (a large land bank) across the U.S., UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, Oman, Ireland and Bahrain, and takes title-transfer or consignment fees on nearly every vehicle that passes through its yards. Copart's core insurance salvage business is a scaled, capital-intensive duopoly with RB Global (IAA) as its only comparable competitor, and it is now expanding into wholesale/non-salvage vehicle remarketing following its September 2026 agreement to acquire ACV Auctions for $1.9 billion.

business_model.summary: Copart earns fee-based revenue on essentially every vehicle that moves through its auction platform, primarily under a 'principal' consignment model in which it charges the seller (mostly insurance carriers) a fee for storage, title/DMV processing, transportation and selling services, plus a separate buyer fee paid by the winning bidder. A smaller and more cyclical portion of revenue comes from purchasing vehicles outright (Cash for Cars / CSA / Blue Car programs, wholesale/dealer purchases) and reselling them for its own account, which shows up as 'purchased vehicle' or 'vehicle sales' revenue rather than pure service fee revenue. Because Copart is paid fees regardless of the vehicle's ultimate price (in the standard consignment model), revenue is driven mainly by unit volume (total loss frequency, accident rates, catastrophic weather) and secondarily by average selling price, which affects revenue-share-based fees and purchased-vehicle margins.

revenue_streams.name: Purchased vehicle sales / CSA-Cash for Cars / Blue Car / dealer & wholesale non-insurance
International segment (UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, etc.)
revenue_streams.trend: growing fastest (units +10%, revenue +11.7% in Q4 FY26)

revenue_streams.name: Ancillary services (transportation, title, inspection, Purple Wave construction/ag/fleet auctions)

business_model.customer_type: B2B2C hybrid - sellers are overwhelmingly institutional (insurance carriers ~75-80% of US volume historically, plus dealers, banks, rental/fleet companies, charities); buyers are global, ranging from licensed dismantlers/rebuilders/exporters to the general public
business_model.geographic_mix: US the large majority of revenue and profit; International (UK/Europe, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, Oman, Ireland, Bahrain) roughly 20% of revenue in FY2026 but ~38% of units and ~46% of dollars-of-vehicles-sold from international buyers, reflecting Copart's role as an export hub for global used/salvage vehicle demand

competitive_position.market_position: Co-leader of a U.S. salvage-auction duopoly with RB Global's IAA; historical estimates put Copart at roughly 55-65% share of the US insurance total-loss salvage market versus IAA's ~30-40%, though 2026 data show share momentum reversing in IAA's favor

moat_factors.description: Owning (rather than leasing) a large, geographically dense network of storage/auction yards near major population centers is extremely difficult and slow to replicate, and is critical for responding quickly to catastrophic weather events (hurricanes, wildfires, hail) when insurers need surge capacity

Proprietary online bidding technology and imaging tools created switching costs and efficiency advantages over legacy live-auction models, though IAA/RB Global has closed much of this technology gap in recent years
Scale of buyer base (global dismantlers/exporters) increases auction returns for sellers, reinforcing insurer relationships, while breadth of seller supply attracts more buyers

Multi-year assignment agreements with large national insurers create some stickiness, but carriers can and do reallocate volume between Copart and IAA based on price/service (e.g., Progressive's 2026 shift favoring IAA)
Minimal debt (D/E ~0.01) and strong free cash flow generation give Copart capital flexibility for land purchases, buybacks, and M&A (e.g., ACV) that smaller competitors cannot match

weaknesses: High customer concentration risk: a handful of large national insurers (State Farm, Progressive, Geico, Allstate, etc.) represent an outsized share of US salvage volume, and losing or losing share of a single large account materially moves results

2026 data show Copart losing unit-volume momentum (units down ~2.8% YoY) while RB Global/IAA units grew (+4.7%), driven partly by Progressive shifting a greater share of assignments to IAA and IAA's operational cycle-time improvements

Domestic insurance salvage unit growth is maturing/plateauing after a decade of total-loss-frequency-driven growth, pushing Copart to rely more on price and international/non-insurance channels for growth

ACV Auctions acquisition takes Copart into an adjacent, historically money-losing wholesale marketplace business with integration risk and management's own guidance that the deal is breakeven in year one and not accretive until FY2028

growth_drivers: International expansion - UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland and other markets now all profitable, growing units and revenue faster than the US and serving as an export outlet for global used/salvage vehicle demand

Non-insurance seller diversification - dealers, banks, rental/fleet companies, and directly-purchased vehicles via CSA/Cash for Cars/Blue Car programs, reducing reliance on insurance total-loss volume alone

Rising total loss frequency structurally - increasing vehicle repair costs (ADAS, electronics, computer chips) versus used vehicle values continue to push more accident vehicles to salvage rather than repair, a multi-decade secular tailwind though possibly moderating

M&A into adjacent markets - the pending $1.9B acquisition of ACV Auctions (a digital wholesale/dealer vehicle marketplace) expands Copart beyond salvage into mainstream used-vehicle wholesale, a large addressable market, while ACV continues to operate under existing leadership

Technology/AI investment - management has highlighted AI and automation as strategic priorities to lower costs and differentiate the buying/selling experience, and continued VB3/Copart 360/IntelliSeller platform enhancements
Continued yard/land bank capacity additions to support both catastrophic-event surge capacity and organic volume growth
Pricing/mix - average selling prices rose 3.5% in Q4 FY2026 and 5.5% for full-year FY2026, partially offsetting unit volume softness

business.description: A small number of national insurance carriers drive a large share of US salvage volume; carriers can reallocate business between Copart and IAA/RB Global based on fees, technology, or service levels (e.g., Progressive's 2026 shift toward IAA)

RB Global completed its IAA turnaround; IAA has cut vehicle cycle times ~7 days (13-15% efficiency gain) and reduced backlog ~20%, and 2026 unit growth trends favor IAA (+4.7%) over Copart (-2.8%), suggesting the long era of Copart share gains may be reversing

Copart's largest-ever acquisition ($1.9B) moves it into a new, historically unprofitable wholesale marketplace segment; management guided to breakeven contribution in the first year and accretion not until FY2028

business.risk: Used vehicle price and total loss frequency cyclicality
business.description: Revenue is sensitive to used vehicle values and total loss frequency trends, which can plateau or reverse if repair costs fall relative to vehicle values or if accident rates decline (e.g., improved ADAS/safety features reducing accident frequency over time)

A meaningful share of volume and revenue upside comes from irregular catastrophic weather events (hurricanes, wildfires, hail storms); results can be lumpy and comparisons distorted by prior-year storm activity

financial.description: Growing international segment (UK, Europe, Brazil, Canada, UAE) creates FX translation exposure on revenue and earnings
Company carries very low leverage (D/E ~0.01) and ample cash/FCF, but the $1.9B ACV deal and any further M&A reduce the buyback/dividend capacity and net cash cushion, at least temporarily

regulatory.description: Salvage title laws, end-of-life vehicle recycling rules, and environmental compliance at storage yards vary by state/country and could raise compliance costs

regulatory.risk: Antitrust/competition scrutiny of a two-player market
regulatory.description: The US salvage auction market's duopoly structure (Copart/RB Global) could draw regulatory attention, particularly around further consolidation or exclusive insurer arrangements; the ACV acquisition itself will require regulatory clearance to close
Expanding operations across multiple foreign jurisdictions (UK, Germany, Brazil, UAE, etc.) exposes the company to varied local regulatory regimes

macro.description: Higher new vehicle prices and interest rates have historically supported used vehicle values (benefiting Copart's purchased-vehicle margins and fee bases), but a reversal (falling used car prices, easing rates) could pressure average selling prices
Miles driven and accident frequency correlate with economic activity, fuel prices, and driving patterns (e.g., remote work reduced miles driven post-pandemic)
A meaningful share of Copart's buyer base and vehicle value comes from international/export buyers; tariffs, sanctions, or export restrictions in key buyer markets could affect demand and pricing

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global salvage/total-loss vehicle remarketing industry has grown for decades on rising total loss frequency (vehicle repair costs outpacing used vehicle values due to more complex electronics/ADAS), but US unit growth is showing signs of maturing in 2026 even as international volumes and pricing continue to grow
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - volumes are influenced by miles driven, accident rates, and catastrophic weather (which can create sharp but temporary spikes), while average selling prices track broader used vehicle market cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect - higher rates have historically supported used vehicle values (benefiting purchased-vehicle margins) but also affect new vehicle affordability and fleet/dealer buying behavior; Copart itself carries minimal debt so direct rate sensitivity on financing costs is low
key_input_costs: Real estate/land (acquisition and carrying cost of the yard network)

recent_developments.event: Copart announced a definitive agreement to acquire ACV Auctions, a digital wholesale used-vehicle marketplace, for approximately $1.9 billion ($10.50/share cash, a ~45% premium to ACV's unaffected price), Copart's largest acquisition ever; expected to close by year-end 2026, with ACV continuing to operate under existing leadership

Q4 FY2026 results (quarter ended July 31, 2026): revenue $1.2B (+2.4% YoY) but gross profit -5.5%, operating income -10.6%, and net income -17.4% YoY; diluted EPS $0.35 vs $0.41 prior year, missing on profitability despite a revenue beat

Several sell-side analysts cut price targets following Q4 results and the ACV deal announcement (e.g., HSBC downgraded to Hold with $36 target; Freedom Broker lowered target to $36 from $39); consensus targets range roughly $36-$65 reflecting wide dispersion in views on margin trajectory and ACV integration

Record/elevated total loss frequency continued, aided by late-2024/2025 catastrophic events (Hurricanes Milton and Helene, Los Angeles wildfires), though FY2026 US unit volumes still declined ~2.8% YoY, suggesting share loss to competitors rather than a market-wide slowdown

International segment strength: units sold internationally +10% and international revenue +11.7% in Q4 FY26; international buyers represented ~38% of units and ~46% of dollar volume for the full year, underscoring Copart's role as a global export hub

Competitive dynamic shift: Progressive Insurance (now the #1 US auto insurer) reportedly shifted a greater share of its total-loss assignment volume toward RB Global's IAA (~75% IAA/25% Copart per some reports), while RB Global/IAA reported unit growth of +4.7% YoY versus Copart's -2.8%, following IAA's operational turnaround (cycle times cut ~7 days, backlog down ~20%)

Q3 FY2026 results beat estimates: revenue $1.24B vs $1.2B expected, EPS $0.43 vs $0.41 expected, though unit volumes declined 2.4% YoY, offset by higher average selling prices and international strength

items.period: First year post-close (expected to close by end of calendar 2026)
items.notes: Management explicitly said the deal is expected to be earnings-accretive only starting in FY2028, implying a drag/dilution period through FY2027

items.target: Continued elevated total loss frequency expected to persist
items.notes: Management continues to expect the long-term secular trend of rising total loss frequency (driven by repair cost inflation from ADAS/electronics) to continue, even though reported US units declined in FY2026

items.target: Qualitative commitment to continued automation-driven cost reduction
items.notes: Management elevated AI and automation as a top strategic priority for cost efficiency and competitive differentiation, without providing specific quantitative targets

guidance.management_commentary: Management framed the Q4 FY2026 miss on gross profit/operating income/net income as reflecting a mix shift and competitive/volume pressure in the US insurance channel, while highlighting record or near-record international growth and profitability across all international markets as evidence the growth algorithm is intact outside the US. Management characterized the ACV Auctions deal as a strategic expansion into the broader wholesale/dealer vehicle marketplace adjacent to its core salvage business, acknowledging it would be roughly breakeven in year one with accretion expected by FY2028, and reiterated confidence in the long-term secular total-loss-frequency growth thesis despite near-term US volume softness attributed in part to competitive dynamics with RB Global/IAA.

bull_case: Duopoly market structure with a scaled, hard-to-replicate land bank of auction/storage yards provides durable competitive advantage and pricing power over the long run

International segment (UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, etc.) is now profitable in all markets and growing units/revenue faster than the US, providing a second growth engine and export demand outlet

Secular total-loss-frequency tailwind remains intact structurally as vehicles become more expensive to repair (ADAS, electronics) relative to their value, supporting long-term volume growth even if near-term US trends are soft

Extremely strong balance sheet (D/E ~0.01, minimal debt) and consistent free cash flow generation give Copart capital flexibility for opportunistic M&A (ACV), land purchases, and shareholder returns without financial strain

ACV Auctions acquisition expands Copart's addressable market into mainstream wholesale/dealer vehicle remarketing, a much larger market than salvage alone, with potential long-term cross-sell and technology synergies
bear_case: 2026 data show Copart losing unit-volume momentum and share to a resurgent RB Global/IAA, which has closed operational gaps (cycle times, backlog) and is winning incremental insurer assignment volume (e.g., Progressive shift), challenging the thesis of an unassailable moat

Q4 FY2026 results showed a meaningful profitability miss (gross profit -5.5%, operating income -10.6%, net income -17.4% YoY) despite a revenue beat, suggesting margin/mix pressure in the core US business

ACV Auctions is Copart's largest-ever acquisition at $1.9B into a historically unprofitable, unproven-at-scale adjacent business, with management itself guiding to breakeven (not accretive) contribution through FY2027 and integration risk given ACV's separate leadership and technology stack

US domestic insurance salvage volumes appear to be plateauing/declining, meaning future growth increasingly depends on pricing, international expansion, and non-insurance sellers rather than the core secular driver that fueled the past decade's growth

Premium valuation (historically trading at a premium multiple reflecting best-in-class moat and growth) leaves little room for error if competitive share losses, margin compression, or ACV integration issues persist, as reflected in several analyst price target cuts following the September 2026 earnings/ACV announcement
